subject: Dedicated carve + resource handoff for HealthScale pilot
messages:
From: Soojin Lee <soojin@redwood.com>
To: Marcus Lin <marcus@redwood.com>, Evelyn Hart <evelyn@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik@redwood.com>, Helen Park <helen@healthscale.ai>
Cc: procurement@healthscale.ai
Date: 2028-07-12T09:12:00-07:00
Subject: Dedicated carve + resource handoff for HealthScale pilot

Hi all —

HealthScale is greenlit for a 6-week production pilot (customer success note attached elsewhere). They need a small dedicated footprint with strict eviction guardrails and a pinned model version for consistency. High-level ask: carve a contiguous slice of GPUs (approx 8 A100-equivalent slots) from our "dedicated-pool-2" for 2028-07-25 through 2028-09-05, with an autoscale exception to keep min_nodes at 2 during business hours (08:00-20:00 PT) to avoid cold-start variance.

Key constraints from the customer: 99.9% availability target, pinned model v2028-07-01, prefix KV caching enabled, and isolation for logs. Procurement (copied) will need a quote and SOC2 evidence.

Action items I need from infra/product:
- Marcus: feasibility and carving procedure, expected impact on the pool and failover plan
- Evelyn: network isolation and cost breakdown for a reserved slice + exception
- Karthik: recommended autoscale policy change (we discussed min_nodes previously) and rollback plan

I'm attaching an initial carve_scope.xlsx to capture exact slot mappings and the SLA exception PDF for internal sign-off. Happy to jump on a 30-min sync if helpful.

Thanks,
Soojin
Soojin Lee
Account Lead, Redwood Inference
soojin@redwood.com

Attachments: carve_scope.xlsx (spreadsheet stub), sla-exception-request.pdf (pdf stub)

From: Marcus Lin <marcus@redwood.com>
To: Soojin Lee <soojin@redwood.com>, Evelyn Hart <evelyn@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik@redwood.com>, Helen Park <helen@healthscale.ai>
Date: 2028-07-12T11:03:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Dedicated carve + resource handoff for HealthScale pilot

Thanks Soojin — quick read-through. We can carve 8 A100-equivalent slots but need to lock the following before we schedule the operation:

1) Exact peak token/sec and average sequence length so we can size KV caches and kernel selection.
2) Confirmation on whether GPU affinity must be contiguous (ranges) or can be non-contiguous with soft affinity. Contiguous reduces fragmentation but may require draining nodes.
3) Billing code / cost center so finance can tag the reservation (Karthik/Evelyn, please advise).

Operational notes: carving contiguous slots will require a brief maintenance window (~15–30m) per affected host; we can batch drains overnight. For the autoscale exception, I agree to set min_nodes=2 during 08:00-20:00 PT; outside that window standard autoscaling applies. We'll need a canary rollout first (1 day) to validate model v2028-07-01 under the reserved lane.

I'll draft an infra runbook and a rollback play (evict to burst lane + throttled ingress). Dropping a first-pass resource map into carve_scope.xlsx and will update.

—Marcus
Marcus Lin
Infrastructure Lead, Redwood Inference
marcus@redwood.com

From: Evelyn Hart <evelyn@redwood.com>
To: Marcus Lin <marcus@redwood.com>, Soojin Lee <soojin@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik@redwood.com>, Helen Park <helen@healthscale.ai>
Date: 2028-07-13T08:21:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Dedicated carve + resource handoff for HealthScale pilot

Looping in some security/ops considerations:

- Network isolation: HealthScale wants isolated logging; we can provide a dedicated VPC subnet and a read-only delivery stream to their logging endpoint. Need SOC2 attestation; Helen/procurement, can you confirm the endpoint and retention requirements?
- Cost: A 6-week carve plus autoscale exception will be billed as Reserved Slice + Exception Premium. Ballpark estimate for 8 A100-equivalent slots is attached to carve_scope.xlsx (sheet: cost_estimate).
- Canary: recommend a 48-hour canary with synthetic workloads before onboarding production traffic. If any P99 latency delta > 60ms we abort and investigate.

Also: if contiguous slots are required and we must drain hosts, please schedule drains during the maintenance window July 23–24. Marcus, can you confirm scheduling constraints?

Evelyn
Evelyn Hart
Head of Reliability & Ops, Redwood Inference
evelyn@redwood.com

From: Karthik Iyer <karthik@redwood.com>
To: Soojin Lee <soojin@redwood.com>, Marcus Lin <marcus@redwood.com>, Evelyn Hart <evelyn@redwood.com>, Helen Park <helen@healthscale.ai>
Date: 2028-07-13T13:45:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Dedicated carve + resource handoff for HealthScale pilot

Two quick suggestions from the runtime/serving side:

1) Instead of strictly pinned contiguous carve, propose a hybrid: reserve 6 contiguous slots + 2 burst-capable non-contiguous slots. That gives us a safety cushion without heavy draining. Customer sees a deterministic lane for most traffic and burst capacity for spikes.

2) Autoscale exception: implement as policy flag 'pilot_mode' with min_nodes=2 and prewarmed_kv=true. The flag can be toggled per-route and audited. This is safer than permanent policy changes and lets us rollback instantly.

I'll prepare the pilot_mode implementation notes and a short migration plan to remove the flag after the pilot. Also, please route invoice/billing info to finance@redwood.com in carve_scope.xlsx.

-karthik

From: Soojin Lee <soojin@redwood.com>
To: Helen Park <helen@healthscale.ai>, procurement@healthscale.ai
Cc: Marcus Lin <marcus@redwood.com>, Evelyn Hart <evelyn@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik@redwood.com>
Date: 2028-07-15T16:31:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Dedicated carve + resource handoff for HealthScale pilot

Helen / Procurement team — thanks for the quick responses. Summary & next steps: 

1) HealthScale to confirm peak tokens/sec and average seq length by EOD 2028-07-18 so Marcus can finalize the carve mapping.
2) Infra (Marcus): draft runbook, schedule host drains July 23–24 if contiguous carve needed; prepare rollback to burst lane.
3) Ops (Evelyn): prepare the VPC subnet and SOC2 evidence packet; confirm cost estimate in carve_scope.xlsx.
4) Runtime (Karthik): implement pilot_mode flag and a 48-hour canary plan (will own the canary results).
5) Soojin/CS will deliver customer signature on the MOU and procurement will request formal quote (procurement@healthscale.ai).

I've attached the current carve_scope.xlsx with the proposed 6+2 hybrid mapping and a short SLA exception request PDF for internal approval. Marcus/Evelyn/Karthik — please mark any redlines in the spreadsheet by 07/18 so I can coordinate the formal quote.

I'll schedule a 30-min alignment call for 07/19 at 10:00 PT if that works for infra/ops.

Best,
Soojin
Account Lead, Redwood Inference
soojin@redwood.com

Attachments: carve_scope.xlsx (updated), sla-exception-request.pdf (updated)
